title: Beyond Antioxidants: Phytochemicals in Cardiometabolic Disease Through the Gut Microbiota-Epigenetic-Senescence-Inflammasome Axis
content: Cardiometabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), represent a major global health burden. Their pathogenesis involves interconnected processes, including oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, gut microbiota dysbiosis, epigenetic alterations, and cellular senescence. Phytochemicals, naturally occurring bioactive compounds found in plant-derived foods, have traditionally been studied for their antioxidant properties. However, emerging evidence suggests that their effects extend beyond free-radical scavenging and involve the modulation of interconnected molecular pathways. This review explores the potential role of phytochemicals in cardiometabolic health, focusing on the gut microbiota- epigenetics- senescence- inflammasome axis. Phytochemicals interact bidirectionally with the gut microbiota, influencing microbial composition, intestinal barrier integrity, and the production of bioactive metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids. These interactions may affect epigenetic regulation, inflammatory signaling, and cellular senescence. Particular attention is given to the senescence-associated secretory phenotype and its interplay with inflammasome activation, especially the NLRP3 inflammasome, which may contribute to chronic inflammation and metabolic dysfunction. Nevertheless, clinical translation remains challenging because of differences in bioavailability, interindividual variability in gut microbiota composition, and the predominance of preclinical evidence for several proposed mechanisms. Understanding these interactions may help identify novel preventive and therapeutic strategies for cardiometabolic diseases and guide future research toward targeted, microbiota-informed nutritional interventions.
